text:
Network requests fail all the time. A server times out, a connection drops, or a busy service sends back an error for a request that would have gone through a second later. You can retry, of course, but hand-written retry loops are easy to get subtly wrong, and copying one into every corner of a codebase gets old fast.

This library does the retrying for you. If an HTTP request fails, it tries again with exponential backoff: each failure makes the next wait longer, which gives a struggling server room to recover. It also adds jitter, a random offset on each delay, so a crowd of clients doesn't retry in lockstep and slam the server at the same instant.

There are no dependencies. Installing it pulls in nothing else, which means no version conflicts to sort out and no extra packages to audit.

We're at version 0.9 right now, with 94% test coverage. Since it hasn't hit 1.0 yet, the API might still change. Bug reports and feedback are very welcome. If you run into an edge case it doesn't handle, open an issue and we'll try to cover it before the stable release.
